## Package limes

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes"`

<a id="limes.DefaultRevocationCacheEntries"></a>

### limes.DefaultRevocationCacheEntries

```go
const DefaultRevocationCacheEntries = 100_000
```

DefaultRevocationCacheEntries bounds the cache. Past it, the oldest entry makes room for the new one: a flood of distinct ids costs extra lookups and never unbounded memory. It does evict other callers' answers of the same kind, each costing one lookup more; the other kinds' are kept (RevocationCacheConfig.MaxEntries).

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.DefaultRevocationCacheTTL"></a>

### limes.DefaultRevocationCacheTTL

```go
const DefaultRevocationCacheTTL = 2 * time.Second
```

DefaultRevocationCacheTTL bounds how long a cached answer is served. A revocation therefore takes effect within this window on every verifier that did not perform it and hears no signal of it. It suits the requests of one exchange; a token verified less often — once per step of an agent — wants a longer bound while a revocation signal vouches for the cache: RevocationCacheConfig.SyncedTTL.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.MaxRevocationCacheStale"></a>

### limes.MaxRevocationCacheStale

```go
const MaxRevocationCacheStale = time.Hour
```

MaxRevocationCacheStale bounds RevocationCacheConfig.MaxStale. A stale answer leaves a revocation unseen while the upstream is down, so an outage longer than this is one the cache fails closed through.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.MaxRevocationCacheSyncedTTL"></a>

### limes.MaxRevocationCacheSyncedTTL

```go
const MaxRevocationCacheSyncedTTL = 24 * time.Hour
```

MaxRevocationCacheSyncedTTL bounds RevocationCacheConfig.SyncedTTL. A signal that listens and still carries nothing — a notification its source never sends — leaves a revocation unseen for as long as the bound in force, so even a synced cache asks again within a day.

<a id="limes.ErrNoRevocationLineage"></a>

### limes.ErrNoRevocationLineage

```go
var ErrNoRevocationLineage = errors.New("limes: the revocation upstream names no lineage")
```

ErrNoRevocationLineage is NewRevocationCache refusing, under RevocationCacheConfig.RequireLineage, a Capabilities upstream that is no RevocationLineageLookup, and RevocationCache.RevocationLineage answering over such an upstream: a verifier that requires a record, given a lookup of yours that wraps such a cache, fails the verification with it.

<a id="limes.BiscuitCopy"></a>

### limes.BiscuitCopy

```go
type BiscuitCopy struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

BiscuitCopy identifies one copy of a capability's Biscuit. Only Verifier.BiscuitCopy makes one, from a token whose signature chain it checked, so the revocation id and the capability it is revoked under always belong together: a caller cannot name another tenant's copy under its own capability. The zero BiscuitCopy names nothing.

<sub>[biscuit_revocation.go](../../biscuit_revocation.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.BiscuitRevocationStore"></a>

### limes.BiscuitRevocationStore

```go
type BiscuitRevocationStore interface {
	BiscuitRevocationLookup

	// RevokeBiscuit lists the revocation id of one Biscuit copy, under the
	// capability the copy belongs to — the pair Verifier.BiscuitCopy read
	// from the token, which no caller can assemble — and says whether the
	// copy had an entry already. Idempotent: a repeat writes nothing, keeps
	// the first entry and reports it with AlreadyRevoked. Returns
	// ErrNotFound when the capability is not on record — or not visible to
	// the caller — so a caller cannot revoke a copy of a capability it cannot
	// see, and ErrInvalidRequest for a request naming no copy.
	RevokeBiscuit(ctx context.Context, req RevokeBiscuitRequest) (RevokeBiscuitResult, error)

	// GetBiscuitRevocation reads back what RevokeBiscuit wrote for one copy,
	// under the capability it was revoked under. ErrNotFound when the copy is
	// not revoked under that capability, or the capability is one the caller
	// cannot see; ErrInvalidRequest for the zero BiscuitCopy.
	GetBiscuitRevocation(ctx context.Context, copy BiscuitCopy) (BiscuitRevocation, error)
}
```

BiscuitRevocationStore persists revoked Biscuit copies. It is separate from Store so that a consumer without Biscuits implements nothing more.

<a id="limes.BulkRevoker"></a>

### limes.BulkRevoker

```go
type BulkRevoker interface {
	// RevokeMatching writes a revocation entry, not cascaded, for at most
	// req.BatchLimit() capabilities of req.TenantID — or, with AllTenants,
	// of every tenant — that match every selector req names and have no
	// entry of their own, in order of tenant and id, and reports how many,
	// in which tenants, and whether more may match. It refuses what
	// RevokeMatchingRequest.Validate refuses, a call scoped to another
	// tenant, and an AllTenants call under a scope that does not admit
	// writing every tenant, as ErrScopeMismatch.
	RevokeMatching(ctx context.Context, req RevokeMatchingRequest) (RevokeMatchingResult, error)
}
```

BulkRevoker revokes every capability of a tenant that matches a subject, an on-behalf-of, a client, a session, an agent run or a subject issuer — or of every tenant that matches a client, a session or a subject issuer — in batches, as Revoke revokes one: an entry for each that has none, and every descendant stopped through its lineage. A store that records sessions and subject issuers (InsertRequest.Session, InsertRequest.SubjectIssuer) implements it; memstore and pgstore do.

<a id="limes.RevocationCache"></a>

### limes.RevocationCache

```go
type RevocationCache struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

RevocationCache is a small in-memory cache for revocation answers: of a capability, IsRevoked, and of a Biscuit copy, IsBiscuitRevoked. One cache serves both, so one Clear, wired to a revocation notification, reaches every answer a verifier holds.

A cached answer about a capability is also an answer about its ancestors, so revoking a parent reaches a child's cached "live" entry only when that entry expires — within the TTL, like any other revocation seen from another process — or when Clear drops it. ClearRevoked drops only the answers a revocation of some ids outdates, when the capabilities' upstream is a RevocationLineageLookup and the cache knows each answer's ancestors; over any other upstream it is Clear.

Concurrent misses for the same question share one upstream call.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevocationCache.Clear"></a>

#### limes.RevocationCache.Clear

```go
func (c *RevocationCache) Clear()
```

Clear drops every entry. A consumer that learns of a revocation from elsewhere — a database notification, a message bus — calls it so the next check goes upstream at once instead of waiting out the TTL. It drops everything, not only the revoked id, because an answer cached for a descendant is also an answer about the revoked ancestor.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevocationCache.ClearRevoked"></a>

#### limes.RevocationCache.ClearRevoked

```go
func (c *RevocationCache) ClearRevoked(ids ...uuid.UUID)
```

ClearRevoked drops what a revocation of ids outdates: each one's cached "not revoked" answer and that of every descendant the cache holds one for, which it knows by the ancestors its upstream named. Every other answer stays, Biscuit copies' among them — revoking a capability revokes no copy's own id — so a consumer that revokes often keeps the answers it did not touch. A lookup in flight when it runs caches nothing, as with Clear. Over an upstream that is no RevocationLineageLookup it is Clear: the cache cannot tell a descendant from any other id. A Biscuit copy's revocation still takes Clear. Named no id, it drops nothing.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevocationCache.IsBiscuitRevoked"></a>

#### limes.RevocationCache.IsBiscuitRevoked

```go
func (c *RevocationCache) IsBiscuitRevoked(ctx context.Context, revocationIDs [][]byte) (bool, error)
```

IsBiscuitRevoked answers from the cache for each id that has a fresh answer, and asks upstream about all the others in one lookup, shared by every concurrent caller asking about the same ones. A token is revoked when any of its ids is: the ids a token shares with the copies it was attenuated from stay cached, so a fresh attenuation — which anyone holding a copy can make offline — costs one lookup for its new block, and a token of blocks the cache has never seen one lookup in all, not one per block. A "live" answer is then cached for each of them; a "revoked" one for that set and for the token's own ids, as upstream does not say which id it is, and it holds for every copy attenuated from the token. An upstream error is returned and never cached.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevocationCache.RevocationLineage"></a>

#### limes.RevocationCache.RevocationLineage

```go
func (c *RevocationCache) RevocationLineage(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (RevocationAnswer, error)
```

RevocationLineage answers as its upstream's RevocationLineage does, from the cache: a "not revoked" answer with the ancestors it was read with, and an id the upstream has no record of as ErrNotFound, which it then answers from unrecorded for TTL rather than ask the upstream again on every request. A cache whose Capabilities is no RevocationLineageLookup names no lineage, and returns ErrNoRevocationLineage rather than an answer that could not tell an id not on record from one not revoked. So a cache, or a decorator forwarding to one, is a RevocationLineageLookup to a verifier that requires a record.

<a id="limes.RevocationCacheConfig"></a>

### limes.RevocationCacheConfig

```go
type RevocationCacheConfig struct {
	// Capabilities answers IsRevoked for what the cache does not hold.
	// Required. When it is a RevocationLineageLookup the cache asks
	// RevocationLineage in place of IsRevoked, and ClearRevoked drops only
	// what a revocation outdates. A decorator of a store keeps that only by
	// having the method itself: a struct embedding limes.Store has no
	// RevocationLineage to promote, so it forwards one —
	//
	//	func (c counting) RevocationLineage(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (limes.RevocationAnswer, error) {
	//		return c.lineage.RevocationLineage(ctx, id)
	//	}
	//
	// — and counts there what it counts in IsRevoked.
	Capabilities RevocationLookup
	// RequireLineage refuses a Capabilities that is no
	// RevocationLineageLookup, with ErrNoRevocationLineage, where the cache
	// would otherwise clear whole on every ClearRevoked.
	RequireLineage bool
	// Biscuits answers IsBiscuitRevoked for what the cache does not hold.
	// Optional: without it the cache refuses every Biscuit question, and
	// NewVerifier refuses it as BiscuitConfig.Revocations. A store that
	// implements both, as pgstore's does, is passed as both. A nil pointer
	// held here is refused.
	Biscuits BiscuitRevocationLookup
	// TTL is how long an answer is served. Zero: DefaultRevocationCacheTTL.
	// It bounds how long a revocation may go unseen where no revocation
	// signal reaches the cache.
	TTL time.Duration
	// SyncedTTL is how long an answer is served while revocation signals
	// vouch for the cache: while at least one RevocationSignal is open and
	// every open one listens, as pgstore.RevocationWatcher's does while
	// its connection listens. A revocation then reaches the cache at once,
	// so the TTL can be long. It covers only the answers read since the
	// last signal began to listen; TTL bounds every other, and every
	// answer while the signals do not vouch, those cached under SyncedTTL
	// among them. Zero: TTL; shorter than TTL, or longer than
	// MaxRevocationCacheSyncedTTL, is refused.
	SyncedTTL time.Duration
	// MaxEntries bounds each kind of answer on its own — about a
	// capability, about one not on record, about a Biscuit — so a flood of
	// one never evicts another. Zero: DefaultRevocationCacheEntries. A Biscuit
	// answer is one entry per revocation id, keyed by the id, a block
	// signature, and one per set of ids asked about together, keyed by a
	// SHA-256 digest of the set, whatever its size. Over a RevocationLineageLookup a
	// capability's "not revoked" answer keeps its ancestors' ids beside it,
	// up to MaxDelegationDepth of them, and again in an index ClearRevoked
	// reads them by: about 32 bytes per generation, so a full cache of
	// chains 64 deep holds some 200 MB of them at the default bound, against
	// 64 to 160 bytes for chains two to five deep. Each kind is spread over
	// shards with a lock each, and past the bound a shard drops its oldest
	// answer: the oldest of all only in a cache small enough to be one
	// shard.
	MaxEntries int
	// MaxStale is how long past the TTL in force an answer stands in for
	// an upstream that fails: the question is answered as it was then, in
	// place of the failure, counted (RevocationCacheCounts.Stale) and
	// logged. Zero: never, the cache failing closed — every failure
	// returned, as a verifier refuses on it. A revocation the upstream
	// holds goes unseen for as long, so it trades revocation latency for
	// availability through a short outage of the store; ErrNotFound, an
	// answer, is never covered, nor a caller whose context ended; nor, while
	// a revoked answer dropped to make room (MaxEntries) would still be
	// kept, a live answer about a delegated capability or about a Biscuit's
	// revocation ids asked together. A
	// Biscuit is covered when its revocation ids are asked about together
	// as before. Negative, or longer than MaxRevocationCacheStale, is
	// refused.
	MaxStale time.Duration
	// Logger logs every stale answer served, at WARN. Nil: slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Now is the clock. Nil: time.Now.
	Now func() time.Time
}
```

RevocationCacheConfig configures a RevocationCache.

<a id="limes.RevocationCacheCounts"></a>

### limes.RevocationCacheCounts

```go
type RevocationCacheCounts struct {
	// Hits counts the questions answered from the cache, Misses the ones
	// that waited on an upstream lookup: each question is one or the
	// other, but for a capability question answered from Unrecorded, which
	// counts there alone. A Biscuit question is a hit only when every id of the token
	// has a fresh answer.
	Hits, Misses uint64
	// Lookups counts the upstream lookups run for the misses: fewer than
	// Misses when concurrent misses share one.
	Lookups uint64
	// Evictions counts the live answers dropped to stay within
	// RevocationCacheConfig.MaxEntries: a count that keeps growing says
	// the bound is too small for the ids in use.
	Evictions uint64
	// Stale counts the stale answers served in place of an upstream's
	// failure (RevocationCacheConfig.MaxStale): growing, the upstream is
	// failing and revocations may go unseen.
	Stale uint64
	// Entries is how many answers the cache holds, fresh or not yet
	// swept.
	Entries int
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

RevocationCacheCounts is one kind of answer's share of RevocationCacheStats.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevocationCacheStats"></a>

### limes.RevocationCacheStats

```go
type RevocationCacheStats struct {
	// Capabilities counts the IsRevoked questions.
	Capabilities RevocationCacheCounts
	// Biscuits counts the IsBiscuitRevoked questions.
	Biscuits RevocationCacheCounts
	// Unrecorded counts the answers about a capability the upstream has no
	// record of, which the cache keeps for TTL apart from Capabilities':
	// Hits the questions answered from them, which Capabilities does not
	// count, Entries how many it holds, Evictions those dropped to stay
	// within MaxEntries. Its Misses, Lookups and Stale stay zero: the
	// question that found no record is a miss of Capabilities. Zero over
	// an upstream that names no lineage (Lineage), which tells no record
	// apart.
	Unrecorded RevocationCacheCounts
	// Clears counts the calls to Clear, and NarrowClears those to
	// ClearRevoked that dropped only what a revocation outdates; one over
	// an upstream that names no ancestors is a Clear.
	Clears, NarrowClears uint64
	// ClearsWithoutLineage counts the calls to ClearRevoked that cleared
	// whole, as the upstream names no lineage: a part of Clears, apart from
	// a Clear asked for. Growing, narrow invalidation is off (Lineage).
	ClearsWithoutLineage uint64
	// Synced reports that revocation signals vouch for the cache now —
	// every open one listens, and its lease holds — and SyncedTTL bounds
	// the answers read since they began to listen; false, TTL bounds every
	// one. Syncs counts the signals' Listening, a Renew after the lease
	// lapsed, and the Close that left every open signal listening: the
	// watchers' connections, their first and every reconnect. None clears.
	Synced bool
	Syncs  uint64
	// SyncsLost counts the signals' NotListening and the leases that
	// lapsed unrenewed, each once, and LastSyncLoss is the time of the
	// last: zero, none yet. A lapse is counted when the cache next looks,
	// Stats among the times it does, at the time the lease lapsed. A count
	// growing as fast as Syncs says the watcher keeps losing its
	// connection; one growing with no NotListening, that a signal stopped
	// renewing.
	SyncsLost    uint64
	LastSyncLoss time.Time
	// Signals counts the notifications revocation signals passed on
	// (Revoked, RevokedAll), and SignalsWhole those that named no id and
	// cleared whole (RevokedAll), a part of Clears. Clears less
	// SignalsWhole and ClearsWithoutLineage is the Clears the consumer
	// asked for itself.
	Signals, SignalsWhole uint64
	// Lineage reports that the cache's upstream names each answer's
	// ancestors, so ClearRevoked drops only what a revocation outdates;
	// false, every ClearRevoked is a Clear.
	Lineage bool
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

RevocationCacheStats is what a RevocationCache has counted since it was made, and what it holds now: of each kind of answer, and its clears. The counts only grow, so a metrics exporter reads them as counters (otelmetric.InstrumentRevocationCache).

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevocationLineageLookup"></a>

### limes.RevocationLineageLookup

```go
type RevocationLineageLookup interface {
	RevocationLookup
	// RevocationLineage answers as IsRevoked does, and names the ancestors
	// of id still on record that the answer read: every one, when id is
	// not revoked. An id not on record is ErrNotFound: the cache answers
	// it not revoked, as IsRevoked does — or, to a verifier without
	// VerifierConfig.AllowUnrecorded, not on record — and keeps that answer
	// for TTL apart from the others. One that answers such an id not
	// revoked instead is cached as any other, and defeats
	// the record check without a word: NewVerifier cannot tell
	// it from one that keeps this contract, which storetest checks.
	RevocationLineage(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (RevocationAnswer, error)
}
```

RevocationLineageLookup is a RevocationLookup that also names the ancestors an answer covers. A RevocationCache is one, and over one keeps them beside each "not revoked" answer, so ClearRevoked drops only the answers a revocation outdates rather than every one. memstore's Store and pgstore's are each one.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevocationLookup"></a>

### limes.RevocationLookup

```go
type RevocationLookup interface {
	// IsRevoked reports whether id, or any ancestor of it, is revoked. An
	// error is no answer: the verifier refuses rather than assume not.
	IsRevoked(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (bool, error)
}
```

RevocationLookup is the seam the cache wraps. A persistent store implements it; tests substitute a stub. Like Store.IsRevoked, it answers for the capability's whole delegation chain.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevocationSignal"></a>

### limes.RevocationSignal

```go
type RevocationSignal struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

RevocationSignal is one revocation signal's hold on a RevocationCache — a watcher's: it says through it when it listens and what it hears, and closes it when it stops for good. The cache serves SyncedTTL while at least one signal is open and every open one listens, since a revocation the one not listening would have carried goes unheard. A signal opened later is not waited for: start the watchers that feed one cache together. After Close, every call does nothing.

A signal vouches for the cache for a lease at a time: Listening grants the first, and the signal Renews it each time it knows itself still listening — a notification heard, a connection checked. One that stops without a word, its goroutine stuck or gone, lets its lease lapse, and the cache falls back to TTL then, as at NotListening, rather than serve SyncedTTL on the word of a signal no longer there.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevocationSignal.Close"></a>

#### limes.RevocationSignal.Close

```go
func (s *RevocationSignal) Close()
```

Close ends the signal: it no longer counts toward synced, and the cache is synced again only while another open signal listens. Closing the one signal that kept the cache on TTL — lost, never listening, or its lease lapsed — counts as a Listening of the others: what was cached while it was down may miss a revocation it would have carried, so SyncedTTL covers only the answers read from then on. Once is enough; again, it does nothing.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevocationSignal.Listening"></a>

#### limes.RevocationSignal.Listening

```go
func (s *RevocationSignal) Listening(lease time.Duration)
```

Listening says the signal reaches the cache from now on, at each connection a watcher opens, and counts toward synced for lease: the signal Renews it before it lapses, or the cache falls back to TTL. A lease that is not positive vouches for nothing. Again while listening, it is a reconnect, and counts once.

A revocation made while nothing listened sent a signal nobody heard, so an answer read before now may have missed one: SyncedTTL covers only the answers read from now on, and every older one stays on TTL, from when it was read, as while no signal vouched. That is as long as such an answer may be served wherever no signal reaches the cache at all, so no answer outlives the bound the cache keeps without one; nothing is dropped, and a connection that flaps leaves every verifier's answers in place rather than send them all to the store at once as it recovers. A revocation made in the gap shows within TTL of the answer it outdates, not at the reconnect.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevocationSignal.NotListening"></a>

#### limes.RevocationSignal.NotListening

```go
func (s *RevocationSignal) NotListening()
```

NotListening says the signal stopped: a revocation may now go unheard, so every answer, those cached already among them, is served for TTL alone until it listens again. Not listening, it does nothing; its lease lapsed and counted already, it counts no second loss.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevocationSignal.Renew"></a>

#### limes.RevocationSignal.Renew

```go
func (s *RevocationSignal) Renew()
```

Renew says the signal still listens, as it found just now: it vouches for the cache for its lease again from now. Renewed after its lease lapsed, it is a Listening: the cache was on TTL meanwhile, and SyncedTTL covers only the answers read from now on. Not listening, or listening with no lease, it does nothing: a signal that lost its connection says Listening on the next.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>

```go
func (s *RevocationSignal) Revoked(ids ...uuid.UUID)
```

Revoked is the signal's word that ids were revoked: ClearRevoked of them. Named no id, it does nothing; a revocation it cannot name is RevokedAll.

<sub>[cache.go](../../cache.go)</sub>

```go
func (s *RevocationSignal) RevokedAll()
```

RevokedAll is the signal's word of a revocation it cannot name — a Biscuit copy's, or too many ids to name: Clear.

<sub>[biscuit_revocation.go](../../biscuit_revocation.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevokeMatchingRequest"></a>

### limes.RevokeMatchingRequest

```go
type RevokeMatchingRequest struct {
	// TenantID is the tenant whose capabilities are revoked; AllTenants
	// revokes in every tenant instead. Exactly one of them is required.
	TenantID uuid.UUID
	// AllTenants matches capabilities in every tenant, by ClientID,
	// Session and SubjectIssuer alone: an authorization server's client and
	// an identity provider's session are named by the issuer, which knows no
	// tenant, so one may hold capabilities in many. Subject and OnBehalfOf
	// name a principal only within its tenant, and are refused beside it.
	// Where more than one identity provider issues subject tokens, two may
	// name the same client or session: SubjectIssuer tells them apart.
	AllTenants bool
	// Subject matches a capability's Subject.Subject, the principal it
	// authorises: a user who leaves, an agent retired.
	Subject string
	// OnBehalfOf matches the principal a capability acts for
	// (Capability.OnBehalfOf.Subject): every agent acting for a user.
	OnBehalfOf string
	// ClientID matches a capability's ClientID: a client compromised.
	ClientID string
	// Session matches the identity provider's session a capability was
	// issued under (InsertRequest.Session): one the provider ended, by OIDC
	// back-channel logout say.
	Session string
	// RunID matches the agent run a capability was issued to
	// (Capability.Subject.Agent.RunID): a run gone wrong, whose capabilities
	// issued apart share no lineage. The consumer mints run ids, so they name
	// a run within its tenant alone, and AllTenants refuses it.
	RunID uuid.UUID
	// SubjectIssuer matches the issuer of the token a capability's subject
	// was authenticated by (InsertRequest.SubjectIssuer): with ClientID or
	// Session, one identity provider's client or session where another names
	// the same; alone, every capability of a provider removed. Empty
	// matches any issuer, and none: a capability recorded without one is
	// reached only that way.
	SubjectIssuer string
	// Note and Actor are stored for audit, as on RevokeRequest.
	Note, Actor string
	// Limit bounds the capabilities one call revokes. Zero:
	// DefaultHousekeepingLimit; negative is refused.
	Limit int
}
```

RevokeMatchingRequest names the capabilities of one tenant, or of every tenant, to revoke together (docs/adr/0013-bulk-revocation.md, docs/adr/0014-bulk-revocation-across-tenants.md): every one on record that matches each selector given — at least one — and has no revocation entry of its own yet.

<a id="limes.RevokeMatchingResult"></a>

### limes.RevokeMatchingResult

```go
type RevokeMatchingResult struct {
	// Revoked counts the revocation entries the call wrote.
	Revoked int64
	// Tenants are the tenants the call wrote entries in, in ascending
	// order, for an audit per tenant: the request's alone, or none, without
	// AllTenants.
	Tenants []uuid.UUID
	// More reports a full batch: more may match, so call again until it is
	// false. A capability issued meanwhile, by a client still holding a

}
```

<sub>[bulk_revoke.go](../../bulk_revoke.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Revoker"></a>

### limes.Revoker

```go
type Revoker struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Revoker is the admin plane's way to revoke: one capability, the capabilities matching a selector, or one Biscuit copy, each carried out by the store and logged — revocation is the audit event that matters most — with an event for metrics or an audit sink, and the answers it outdates dropped from a RevocationCache in the same process. It holds no signing key, so a service that revokes needs none, and stands beside the Issuer and the Verifier rather than in either.

Each method returns the store's result and error unchanged. A Revoker is safe for concurrent use.

<sub>[revoker.go](../../revoker.go)</sub>

```go
func NewRevoker(cfg RevokerConfig) (*Revoker, error)
```

NewRevoker validates wiring and returns a ready Revoker. It refuses no Store, and a Store, Bulk or Biscuits holding a nil value.

#### limes.Revoker.Revoke

```go
func (r *Revoker) Revoke(ctx context.Context, req RevokeRequest) (RevokeResult, error)
```

Revoke revokes one capability through the store (RevocationStore.Revoke), then drops what that outdates from the cache, whether or not the store returned an error.

<sub>[revoker.go](../../revoker.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Revoker.RevokeBiscuit"></a>

#### limes.Revoker.RevokeBiscuit

```go
func (r *Revoker) RevokeBiscuit(ctx context.Context, req RevokeBiscuitRequest) (RevokeBiscuitResult, error)
```

RevokeBiscuit revokes one Biscuit copy through the BiscuitRevocationStore, then clears the cache, whether or not it returned an error. Without one it is ErrInvalidConfig. The copy is logged by its capability's id alone.

#### limes.Revoker.RevokeMatching

```go
func (r *Revoker) RevokeMatching(ctx context.Context, req RevokeMatchingRequest) (RevokeMatchingResult, error)
```

RevokeMatching revokes a batch of the capabilities matching req through the BulkRevoker, then clears the cache, whether or not it returned an error. Without one it is ErrInvalidConfig.

<sub>[revoker.go](../../revoker.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevokerConfig"></a>

### limes.RevokerConfig

```go
type RevokerConfig struct {
	// Store revokes one capability. Any Store is one.
	Store RevocationStore

	// Bulk revokes the capabilities matching a selector (RevokeMatching).
	// memstore's and pgstore's Store are one. Nil: RevokeMatching refuses
	// with ErrInvalidConfig.
	Bulk BulkRevoker

	// Biscuits revokes one Biscuit copy (RevokeBiscuit). memstore's and
	// pgstore's Store are one. Nil: RevokeBiscuit refuses with
	// ErrInvalidConfig.
	Biscuits BiscuitRevocationStore

	// Cache is this process's RevocationCache, cleared of what each
	// revocation outdates as soon as the store returns: ClearRevoked of the
	// capability after Revoke, which reaches every descendant the cache
	// holds an answer for; Clear after RevokeMatching, whose result names
	// no capability, and after RevokeBiscuit, as a copy's revocation takes.
	// A store that returns an error is cleared after too: a write may have
	// committed before the error — a context ended, a connection lost on
	// the commit — and a dropped answer costs only a lookup. It reaches no
	// other process's cache: there, a revocation is seen through
	// pgstore.RevocationWatcher or once the cache's TTL runs out. Nil: no
	// cache is cleared.
	Cache *RevocationCache

	// Logger logs every revocation, naming capabilities by id and never
	// logging a token: each call the store carried out at INFO — a repeat
	// that wrote nothing among them — each request it refused at WARN, each
	// call that failed for the server's own reasons at ERROR. Nil:
	// slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger

	// Events are called beside the log, for metrics or an audit sink. The
	// zero RevokerEvents calls nothing.
	Events RevokerEvents
}
```

RevokerConfig is the wiring for NewRevoker.
